author: original (NevaIB)
title: The binomial distribution
bigPicture: The binomial distribution counts successes in a fixed number of independent trials. Check the conditions first, then let the GDC do the arithmetic.

keyIdeas.cue: When is X ~ B(n, p) a suitable model?
keyIdeas.answer: A fixed number n of trials; each trial has two outcomes (success or failure); the probability of success p is constant; the trials are independent.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you find binomial probabilities?
keyIdeas.answer: GDC: binompdf for P(X = r), binomcdf for P(X ≤ r). P(X ≥ r) = 1 − P(X ≤ r − 1); P(X > r) = 1 − P(X ≤ r).
E(X) = np; Var(X) = np(1 − p); standard deviation √(np(1 − p)).

keyTerms.def: number of successes in n independent trials with constant p

misconceptions.right: p changes between draws, so the trials are not independent.

practice.prompt: X ~ B(20, 0.3). Find E(X) and Var(X).
commonErrors: Giving the sd as the variance

practice.prompt: A player scores 70% of penalties, independently. She takes 10 penalties. Find (a) P(exactly 8) (b) P(at least 8).

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.
